Resolves #20511

A component moved across parents now renders in its new parent, so emptying a grid's locked region keeps the header that left it. `Container#insert` flushed a cross-parent move at the lowest common ancestor and widened only that ancestor's update depth. The receiving container could still be a root of its own in that batch, at the depth its previous update had reset it to, and then pruned the newcomer its vnode did not hold yet. The receiver now widens too. Locking a grouped column moves its whole group (AC-2), and the example connects the Neural Link client (AC-3).

Evidence: L2 (real-pointer e2e on `examples/grid/headerGroups`; unit for the receiver's payload and the group-atomic lock) → L2 required (AC-1, AC-2); AC-3 is the example config. No residuals.

## Deltas from ticket
- **The fix is in `container.Base#insert`, not `Wrapper#updateHeaders`.** The ticket's hypothesis, that the retired toolbar's vnode inlines the moved button, does not hold: read through `getConfigs`, every toolbar and the wrapper hold `componentId` references only, before and after. The discriminating state is the receiving toolbar's `updateDepth`. It is -1 at boot, a pending value no update has spent yet, which is why a plain drop passes. After any update it is 1, because `VdomLifecycle` resets the depth to the class default. Restoring it to -1 through `setConfigs` brings the button's `insertNode` back. `beforeSetUpdateDepth` only widens, so the fix is the same one `Component#show()` makes for a mounting child: widen the receiver.
- The trigger is any earlier update of the receiving toolbar, not only the cross-region drop in the matrix sequence: the e2e drags Jan onto Region, a drop the region refuses, before it empties the start region.
- **AC-3's locked-start group is out of this PR.** With a group in both locked regions, no drag can empty one, so AC-1's scenario (matrix row 4A) would have nowhere to run, and the fixture's documented geometry also underpins #20520's and #20517's e2e specs. The ticket's author moved the group to a last-landing leaf after those PRs, beside an ungrouped Region.

## Test Evidence
Red-first on this branch before the fix (`dddeaaf439`): the e2e loses the Region header (2/2 repeats), and the unit spec finds the newcomer as a `neoIgnore` placeholder. With the fix: both green, the e2e 3/3 repeats. Full unit suite: 6585 passed on this branch against 6584 on `origin/dev` (the extra one is `InsertCrossParent`), 0 failed on both. One test that the branch's full run listed as did-not-run (`worker/CanvasGroupLifetimes.spec.mjs:112`) passes 40/40 alone. `test/playwright/e2e/dashboard` + `e2e/grid` + `e2e/tab`: 331 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `CellEditingLockedBodies.spec.mjs:93`, which fails intermittently on `origin/dev` too (at least 2 of 22 local runs there, 1 of 23 on this branch). `HeaderGroups.spec.mjs` with `useAiClient` on: 16/16 over two repeats.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: None.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: None.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: When `Neo.container.Base#insert` performs an atomic cross-parent move and flushes at the lowest common ancestor (`lca`), widening only `lca.updateDepth = -1` is insufficient if the receiving container (`me`) has already completed an earlier update that reset `me._updateDepth` to `1`: boundary planning can still emit `me` as its own update root at depth `1`, causing `TreeBuilder` to prune the newly moved child (which already has a `vnode` from its previous parent) to `{neoIgnore: true}` and omit its `insertNode` delta. Widening `me.updateDepth = -1` alongside `lca` closes this gap across all `Container` subclasses.
